name: What finish is best for cabinets near a range or cooktop?

mainEntity.name: Which coatings are better at resisting heat, grease, and repeated cleaning around cooking areas?
mainEntity.text: Which coatings are better at resisting heat, grease, and repeated cleaning around cooking areas?

acceptedAnswer.text: Cabinetry near a cooktop experiences more heat, steam, grease, and cleaning than other parts of the kitchen. A durable, well-cured finish is important, but the cabinet design also needs proper spacing, ventilation, and protection from direct burner exposure. Catalyzed lacquer and conversion varnish are commonly chosen because they create a harder, more resistant surface than basic paint. That said, no finish should be expected to survive direct flame contact or extreme radiant heat. If the layout places cabinets close to the range, ask whether a heat shield, metal liner, or adjusted side panel detail is recommended. Grease buildup should also be considered, because some finishes clean more easily without dulling. The best result comes from combining the right finish with smart layout planning, not from coating alone.
acceptedAnswer.description: Cabinets near a range should use a durable, heat-tolerant finish system that resists grease and regular wiping, such as catalyzed lacquer or conversion varnish. Heat shields and proper spacing matter as much as the finish itself. Extremely soft coatings or poorly sealed wood can discolor or fail faster near cooking zones.
